spec.name: integrator
spec.intent:
Census @406cd7d0 for source (identical through 2709be8e: only records/ changed since; re-derive any count or line number below if a listed path changed since, and plan architect-position's architect-skills unit is editing deliver/skill.ts concurrently, so cite its lines by content). Pinned to the amended `integrator position` (2709be8e). Realize `integrator position`: the role that makes each landing durable on the shared line, one per bound plan and warm across its waves. At census no role or agent holds it. packages/canon/src/skills/deliver/skill.ts declares `integrator : P ⇀ agent ⟨one per P · runs gate ∧ integrate ∧ carries the state moves self decided, ¬ decides them⟩` with no role behind it (compare `assayer : unit ⇀ agent ⟨role = assayer · …⟩`). It also defines `integrate(unit) ≜ merge artifact(unit) into main`, which the amended design makes wrong. The corpus projects 7 agents (architect, assayer, implementer, kino, mav, nico, planner), and none of them holds it; in practice the architect session did this work itself, which is the descent the architect position forbids.

THE POSITION (every artifact below states this, in the corpus's own register). It merges each unit's commits onto the BOUND PLAN'S INTEGRATION LINE, never main, which is the release line. It runs the project's whole check (deliver's `gate`: every suite, typecheck and build) ONCE per landing, on that combined tree, so the assay reads exactly what will ship: the integrated commit on the plan's line. A unit whose combined tree is red does not stay on the line. The line is left as it was, and the red goes back to the architect. Only when the architect has accepted every unit and closed the plan does it open the PROMOTION of that line to main, which the operator signs off. It never moves main itself, never pushes, and never releases: it opens a pull request when the repository has a forge remote and `gh`, and otherwise it hands the operator the exact git command that promotes. It runs the plan state-move verbs the architect hands it (plan advance, bind and close, verbatim, carrying the architect's --author, --reason and --cause), never choosing one itself. It commits the records/ files they write, together with any design records the architect wrote, by pathspec, on the plan's line. It reports each gate's result to the architect in ONE line: green, or red naming the failing check and its owner (the unit whose outputs the failing check covers). It never decides: it does not accept or reject, amend the design, or choose what is dispatched, which verb runs, or whether a plan is ready to promote. It never builds, edits or repairs a unit: a red gate goes back to the architect, who routes it to the implementer that owns it. It never reads an artifact to judge it, because the assay is the assayer's. A merge is durability, not acceptance. The integration line is the branch the integrator's dispatch names; the plan recommends `plan/<plan name>`, cut from main when the integrator is first dispatched for a bound plan. Plan architect-position (its architect-role and architect-skills units) states the other side of this contract: the architect decides bind, advance and close and runs no plan verb itself, its role sign routes ⟨gate · merge · commit · state-record⟩ ↦ integrator, and deliver gains the law that the integrator is never self.

CHANGE.
(1) New /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share/packages/canon/src/dimensions/role/integrator.ts, `export const integrator: Role`. It is the contract in the form its four siblings use: `integrator ≜ reads⟨…⟩ → writes⟨…⟩`, the stratum line, `reserves ⟨…⟩`, and the prohibitions. Its writes must NOT admit authoring an artifact. The purview judge's rubric (hooks/purview-guardrail.ts, 'a write whose codomain is artifact by a holder whose writes set excludes artifact') must be able to BLOCK a Write or Edit by this holder, while its reserves name the gate, merge-on-green, state-record and commit, so those acts pass. The anchor is `integrator`: it becomes `Agent.holds` through anchorOf (roles/hold.ts:116), which is the key forge routes on.
(2) New /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share/packages/canon/src/roles/integrator.ts, `export const integratorRole: RoleCell`, mirroring roles/assayer.ts and roles/implementer.ts. guardrails: [honesty]. actions: [file-ops], because this is the position whose work IS the vcs clause `main ⇒ green`. objective: `delivery ⟨end-to-end integrated green⟩`. capabilities: WITHOUT software-engineering, which is the structural statement that it does not build (the architect's own omission is the precedent); use verification-testing, operations-delivery, or both. satisficing: satisfice. autonomy: no `principal-self`, and no `handoff`, whose report shape (conclusion, evidence, action-item tail) contradicts the one-line report; the role contract states the one-line report instead. No workflow skill, following the implementer precedent: its decisions are made for it, and the architect's dispatch carries each verb. Every choice carries a comment in the file's own register, as its siblings' choices do.
(3) New /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share/packages/canon/src/agents/integrator.ts, `holds(integratorRole, { name: 'integrator', description, archetype, provenance: { mark } })`, mirroring agents/assayer.ts. The mark is an emoji and hue no other agent uses (census marks: 🏛️ blue, 🔬 red, 🔧 white, 🎬 magenta, ✈️ green, 📐 cyan, 🗺️ yellow). The description is the dispatch router's selection line: it says what the agent does and states the prohibitions out loud, following the assayer's 'NOT A REVIEWER' precedent. The nearest familiar shapes a dispatcher reaches for are a CI bot that also fixes and a release manager that pushes.
(4) /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share/packages/canon/src/skills/deliver/skill.ts, the integration lines ONLY, which Main assigned to this plan. `integrate(unit) ≜ merge artifact(unit) into main ⟨pre gate green on the MERGED tree …⟩` becomes a merge onto the bound plan's integration line, with the gate green on the combined tree. The `integrator` line names its role (`⟨role = integrator · one per P · …⟩`, as the assayer line does) and adds promotion to what it carries. A new `promote(P)` definition and law say that main, the release line, receives the plan's line only when closed(P) ∧ every unit is accepted; the integrator opens the promotion, and the operator signs it off (sign-off ⊨ operator, ¬ self, ¬ integrator). The laws `gate ⊨ integrate ∧ ¬ verify`, `integrate ⊥ judge` (whose trailer reads 'the assay reads artifact(unit) at its landing commit ∵ main moves under a pipelined assay') and `integrator ⊨ ¬ validate` are restated for the plan's line, so the assay reads the integrated commit on the plan's line. The pipeline `deliver ≜ … → advance → close` ends `→ promote ⟨integrator opens · operator signs off⟩`. Every other line belongs to plan architect-position's architect-skills unit: its executor→implementer spellings (including inside these lines), the judge/validate/verify laws, dispatch, fix, WIP/close, the pipeline's other actors, the description, the header comments, and its `integrator ≠ self` law. The description's destination clause ('integrate each landing into main once the project's whole check is green') is this unit's: rewrite where the landing goes (onto the plan's line, with main receiving only a closed, accepted plan through a promotion the operator signs off). architect-skills changes only who does what in that sentence and keeps its destination wording. Whichever plan lands second re-derives this file's census.
(5) /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share/packages/canon/src/hooks/purview-guardrail.ts: the three places that enumerate legitimate routes name the integrator. They are the comment at :34 ('WHAT IT PASSES: a dispatch to a planner, a dispatch to an assayer'), the residue at :47 (`dispatch ↦ plan ∨ assay`), and the denial feedback at :223-228 (in both the route list and the 'Legitimate and NOT blocked' list, a gate run, merge or commit goes to an integrator). Then regenerate /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share/packages/canon/targets/guardrail/purview-guardrail.sh with `pnpm canon:project:targets` (cwd /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share). No other targets/ file may change.
(6) Role routing, at the routes the ruling on note 'the integrator's role-routing tier' names. Until that ruling revises it, this spec encodes the plan's recommendation: omp `task`, claude `sonnet`. /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share/packages/forge/src/adapters/omp/render.ts OMP_NEAREST_ROLE (:250-253) gains `integrator`. /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share/packages/forge/src/adapters/claude/render.ts CLAUDE_ROLE_TIERS (:74-79) gains `integrator`, and its doc comment (:63-73) says why. test/adapters/omp.test.ts (the table at :1213-1229) and test/adapters/claude.test.ts (the it.each at :695-707 and the alias list at :719-723) gain the integrator row. If the ruling is 'no entry', both tables stay unchanged, and the tests instead assert that integrator routes to `default` on omp and emits no model on claude.
(7) Docs. /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share/packages/cli/README.md (:112-114 claude tiers, :135-136 omp aliases) and /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share/packages/forge/README.md (:248-250, :285-288) list the integrator's route. In /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share/docs/role.md the position catalog (:64-65) names five positions, and one new section records the integrator position: what it is, why it exists, the plan's integration line against main as the release line, and that it holds no workflow skill. Plan architect-position's builder-sign unit owns docs/role.md's executor spellings (:157, :160, :205). /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share/docs/commit-gated-on-acceptance-hypothesis.md spells `integrator` (:17, :72) as a measured dispatch practice. It is a dated record and stays unchanged unless a line there claims the position has no holder.
(8) New /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share/.changeset/integrator-position.md: canon minor, plus forge patch if (6) changed a table.
No new test file is expected. If one is added, register it in /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share/packages/canon/test/gate-convicts.test.ts. CLOSING ASSAY (added): deliver states that when every unit of the bound plan is accepted, one assay reads the whole integration line against every concept the plan realizes, before the plan closes and before the integrator opens the promotion to main; an unachieved concept found there is routed like any unit gap. Per-unit assay (at each landing commit) and closing assay (of the whole line) are the assayer's two scopes.
